correctness.rationale: The ellipsoid quadratic form is exactly \(b^{-2}I-(b^{-2}-a^{-2})e_1e_1^{\mathsf T}\). Its compression to a subspace is a scalar operator minus one rank-one term, so the least restricted eigenvalue is \(b^{-2}-(b^{-2}-a^{-2})\|P_Ee_1\|^2\). For Haar codimension-\(n\) subspaces, the complementary squared projection is exactly \(\operatorname{Beta}(n/2,(N-n)/2)\). This proves the distribution. Monotonic inversion gives the CDF, Euler's beta integral gives the moment formula, and the optimal section radius is \(b\) because a subspace contained in \(e_1^\perp\) attains it while every section has radius at least \(b\). The proportional-dimensional limit follows from the exact beta variance.

value.rationale: The one-spike ellipsoid is the canonical minimal anisotropic model for the random-versus-optimal information question emphasized by the source. The result replaces order bounds by a complete finite law in every codimension, gives exact success probabilities and moments, and identifies the high-anisotropy proportional-dimensional limit \(\lambda^{-1/2}\). This makes the source's potentially unavoidable \(\sqrt{N/n}\) loss exact on a natural family and supplies a reusable benchmark for testing general random-section estimates.
